chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from one of his companions, from Amr ibn Shimir, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

When Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) set out intending Basra, he encamped at Al-Rabada. A man from the Muharib tribe came to him and said, 'O Amir al-Mu'minin! I have borne the burdens of my people, and I asked among their groups for sympathy and assistance, but their tongues preceded me with criticism. So order them, O Amir al-Mu'minin, to assist me and urge them to sympathize with me.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Where are they?' He said, 'Those are a group of them, where you see.'

He said, so he spurred his riding animal and it galloped as if it were a male ostrich. Some of his companions galloped in pursuit of it, striving hard but could not catch up. So he arrived at the people, greeted them, and asked them what prevented them from sympathizing with their companion. They complained about him, and he complained about them.

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'A man should maintain ties with his clan, for they are most deserving of his kindness and his hand's support. And the clan should maintain ties with its brother if time strikes him hard and the world turns away from him. Indeed, those who maintain ties and exchange favors are rewarded, and those who cut ties and turn away are burdened (with blame). He said, then he sent off his riding animal and said, 'Resolved.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Title of Imam Ali)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on maintaining ties with relatives and the consequences of severing them?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this narration highlights Imam Ali’s (AS) practical leadership during his campaign to Basra, where he personally verified the clan's refusal to support a deserving member before commanding them. The text underscores the reciprocal nature of *silat al-rahim*, distinguishing between the rewarded mutual support of the connected and the blamed abandonment of the severed, reflecting the Shia emphasis on social justice within the extended family structure.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from one of his companions, from Amro Bin Shimr, from Jabir, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> went out intending Basra (the battle of the Camel), he<sup>asws</sup> encamped at Al-Rabza. So a man from the fighters came over to him<sup>asws</sup>, and he said, ‘O Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>! I bore the burdens (responsibilities) of my people and I asked among their groups for the sympathy and the assistance but their tongues preceded to me with the temper. So order them, O Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> for assisting me and urge them upon sympathising with me’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Where are they?’ So he said, ‘There, a group of them is where you<sup>asws</sup> see’.

So he spurred on his riding animal and galloped it as if it was a male ostrich, and some of his<sup>asws</sup> companions galloped (their animals) in seeking it (his<sup>asws</sup> ride) in hot pursuit but could not catch up. So he<sup>asws</sup> ended up to the group of people and greeted them and asked them what prevent them from sympathising with their companion. So they complained about him, and he complained about them.

So Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘A person should help his clan, for they are closest with the righteousness, and that is in his hands, and the clan should help its brother if the time is hard with him and the world turns away from him. So the maintainers of the relationships, the helpers would be Recompensed, and that the cutters-off of relationships, the ones who turn around would be burdened (with sins)’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> went away with his<sup>asws</sup> riding animal and said: ‘Resolved’.
en.sarwar: 18. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from certain individuals of his people from ‘Amr ibn Shamir from Jabir from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following:

“When Amir al-Mu’minin (Ali ibn abu Talib) (a.s.) left Madina for Basra, on his way he stopped at al-Rabadhah (a place near Jaddah). A man from Muharib (a tribe) came and said, ‘O Amir al-Mu’minin, I have been shouldering many responsibilities for my people and I have asked quite a few of them to help and cooperate with me, instead they have been very harsh to me. O Amir al-Mu’minin, command them to help me and encourage them to cooperate with me.’ The Imam asked, ‘Where are they?’ He said, ‘Those are a few of them as you may see.’

The man has said, ‘The Imam directed his horse to their direction, which began to move faster than trudge. Certain men from his companions followed, but they had difficulty catching up with him, and he would slow down for them until he reached the people and offered them greetings of peace. He asked them about their lack of cooperation with one of their own people. They complained before the Imam and he complained against them.

Amir al- Mu’minin (Ali ibn abu Talib) (a.s.) said, ‘A man must maintain good relations with relatives; they are more deserving of benefitting from his virtuous deeds and achievements. The relatives must maintain good relations with one of their own in times of need when things are against him. Those who maintain good relations with relatives and help financially are rewarded. Those who cut off good relations with relatives and turn away commit a sin.’ The man has said, ‘The Imam then turned his horse around and directed it to move.’”
